item.title: Friouato Caves
item.description:
Details

Identification

  • Feature type: Cave
  • Source: https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friouato_caves

Cave and exploration data

  • Exploration potential: VeryHigh
  • Tourism potential: Low
  • Goes to water: Yes

Diving data

  • Water type: Fresh
  • Tidal: No

References

  • Wikipedia: https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friouato_caves “A cave diving expedition by Exeter University Speleological Society passed two static sumps in 1969 to discover more large chambers and shafts. The system ends in a massive choke of boulders. This may well be the same massive choke of boulders that can be seen at the end of the upstream passages of the nearby Grotte du Chiker; this choke was also discovered in 1969 by the same group of cavers.”
  • Atlas Obscura: https://www.atlasobscura.com/places/friouato-caves UPDATE AS OF APRIL 2024: THE CAVES ARE CLOSED INDEFINENTLY.

Located between the Rif and Middle Atlas mountain ranges just outside the northern city of Taza, “Grotte Friouato,” or the Friouato Caves as they are more widely known, are a collection of subterranean areas that have been explored by many who have visited Taza.
